_evidence: Variant of ring_0043f40d for 0x0043f40d alone (same coherent geometry: 16 lap records, lap end base+0x1600, wrap 0x1600, lap start base, pit end record 21..24; every visited record stays in 0..24), extended to reach the pit-lane wrap/clamp paths of loops 2 and 3. Changes: (1) record 0 draws a flag byte with bit 0x10 OR bit 0x20 (0x20-only values make loop 1 stop at record 0 after wrapping, so loop 2 retraces across the lap end, 0x0043f4df/0x0043f4fd); every lap cycle still ends at record 0, so loop 1 always terminates. (2) the pit/gap records 16..24 draw flags from their own list with bit 0x10 in 1/2 and 0x20 in 1/4 (loop 3 stops there, then its half-way back step crosses the pit start: 0x0043f560/0x0043f590); records 1..15 keep the 1/16 lists. (3) the pit start [0x00891500] is record 16 (lap flows into the pit, loop 1 leaves the lap there: 0x0043f4e7) in a third of the cases, else 17..20. (4) the thresholds 0x00627ac0/0x00627abc (static 0x40, read only here, compared signed with a sign-extended 16-bit 0x0043fab0 result) include values beyond the 16-bit range (0x8000 / -0x8001) so loop 2 is entered and runs to its end (0x0043f506) often, besides 0x40, 0, +-0x200. (5) word +0x16 of record k draws from k*0x400 +- 0x300 (overlapping windows: mostly rising along the lap, so with the sign selector [0x00627b65] (+-word) loop 3 often runs several records forward into the pit or across the lap end before a 0x10 record or a drop, and still drops at the lap wrap and in reverse; any i16 is valid). Loop 3 still ends at a 0x10 record, a value drop, or the pit-end clamp (constant value: drop with [0x00627b04] >= 1). Original evidence: 0x0043f40d (edi = a track-segment record; its caller 0x0043f636 passes lap records base..[0x00866ecc] whose byte +0x73 has bit 1) walks the 0x160-stride segment array at 0x008943a0 with the shared lap/pit advance (lap end [0x00866ecc], wrap by [0x00866ec4] below pit start [0x00891500], clamp below pit end [0x00866ef8]) and walks back with the inverse (wrap forward by [0x00866ec4] under the lap start [0x00891504], clamp at the pit start). Loop 1 (0x0043f433) stops at a +0x73 bit 0x10 (final) or 0x20 record or when edi leaves the lap; loop 2 (0x0043f4b0, after >= 10 steps) retraces loop 1 to its end; loop 3 (0x0043f525) stops at a bit-0x10 record or when +/-word +0x16 minus [0x00627b04] drops below the previous value. So a lap without any 0x10/0x20 record, an incoherent lap/wrap geometry or a car parked at the pit end with [0x00627b04] <= 0 makes the original loop forever (fuzzed geometry faulted/timed out). Domain: one coherent geometry - 16 lap records 0..15 (lap end base+0x1600, wrap 0x1600, lap start base), pit start record 16..20 (16 = lap flows into the pit, otherwise a gap) and pit end 21..24; record 0 always has bit 0x10, so every lap cycle ends; [0x00627b04] is 1..0x100 (static 0x20), so the pit-end clamp ends loop 3. Starts are records 0..23 (pit and gap starts are a superset of the callers' lap starts, needed to reach the pit branches). Every visited record is then 0..23, and 0x0043fab0 also reads the following record, so words +0, +0x16, +0x18 and the flag byte +0x73 of records 0..24 are varied: flags from a list with bit 0x10 or 0x20 in 1/16 each and bit 2 (sign selector) in most, words unconstrained. 0x00627ac0/0x00627abc (static 0x40, read by no other function) are varied over -0x200..0x200. Every pointer stays inside the 25 records, so nothing faults.
